study type: Single center observational retrospective-prospective case control study
exposure: Type of PDA closure (surgical ligation vs. percutaneous transcatheter closure)
outcome: Neurodevelopmental outcomes (Bayley Scales of Infant Development 3rd ed)
Time to achieve room air status
cohort: The study cohort consisted of preterm infants born at <=29 weeks of gestation who either had no hsPDA, underwent surgical ligation, or percutaneous transcatheter closure of the PDA.
finding: Waiting for infants to achieve appropriate size for percutaneous transcatheter closure of the PDA may lead to reduced short-term complications (e.g., earlier enteral feeds, room air status, less vocal cord paralysis) without increasing the risk of neurodevelopmental impairment compared to surgical ligation.
